en.faq_about_desc:
Gobbo Datacron is an {{'open source' link=repo}} set of tools made by {{'alxl' link=alxl}} to help SWTOR players.

The tools are completely offline. None of the information you provide is ever sent to any server, and that information is only ever saved {{'locally' link=localstorage}}. You don't have to take my word for it - here's the {{'source code' link=repo}}, including instructions for self-hosting.
en.faq_calc_config_preamble: SWTOR typically gets new constants for stat calculations with expansions. To future-proof this tool, you can configure these coefficients manually. The default values are confirmed to be correct for at least version {{ver}}
en.faq_calc_findk_preamble: Assuming that '{{%calc_name_limit}}' and '{{%calc_name_expbase}}' are correct, you can provide an accuracy/alacrity {{%calc_name_rating}} and its equivalent {{%calc_name_percentage}} to approximate '{{%calc_name_expdenom}}'
en.faq_gear_acc_desc: If you are playing a damage discipline, getting your accuracy to 110% is your first priority. Otherwise, non-weak enemies will occasionally dodge your abilities, which you can't afford. Anything over 110% is completely wasted. Healers do not need accuracy because they cannot miss a heal, and tanks do not need accuracy because they already start at 110%.
en.faq_gear_alac_title: Alacrity: ~7.5% for consistent 1.4s GCDs (damage & heal disciplines)
en.faq_gear_alac_desc: Alacrity is the most complicated stat in the game, and there's a lot of incorrect information about it out there. While alacrity generally reduces your cooldowns and compresses your over-time effects, the most important benefit is its reduction of the global cooldown (GCD). GCD is always a multiple of 0.1s, and without any alacrity, your GCD will be 1.5s. Starting at 7.143% alacrity, your GCD will sometimes be 1.4s and sometimes be 1.5s. Once you get to about 7.5% alacrity, your GCD will consistently be 1.4s. (Sometimes you will see this "extra" alacrity referred to as lag compensation, but it doesn't have anything to do with lag.) Generally speaking, alacrity beyond the 1.4s GCD is better spent on extra crit; however, if you have a significant alacrity buff, it may be worth some extra alacrity to bring your GCD down another 0.1s during that buff's uptime.
en.faq_gear_crit_desc: Critical improves both critical chance and multiplier. Once your abilities can no longer miss and your GCD is consistently reduced, increasing your critical will usually be more beneficial to your damage/healing than further increasing your alacrity.
en.faq_gear_tank_desc: The two stats that tanks use for survivability are absorb and shield. Shield increases the chance of blocking incoming attacks, and absorb reduces the amount of damage that blocked attacks deal to you. Unlike accuracy and alacrity, hitting exact thresholds for absorb and shield is unimportant. Instead, you want to aim for a rough ratio between absorb and shield (30% absorb : 70% shield for guardian/warrior, 40% absorb : 60% shield for shadow/assassin, 25% absorb : 75% shield for vanguard/powertech). However, tank builds can be quite diverse; if you find that you are far tankier than you need to be for the activities you play, it can be worthwhile to invest in alacrity and crit instead. Note that even if you are gearing for damage, you still want to use your class-appropriate shield generator in your offhand.
